question: Assume the JTB definition of Knowledge, which suggests that "Knowledge is a Justified True Belief". If our only available epistemic states are Knowledge and Belief, what are the two problems JTB runs into? Ignore Gettier problems.

1.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: On the JTB analysis knowledge is a species of true belief.
If the ontology of the mind is closed to just Knowledge and mere Belief,
justification cannot be an independent third epistemic attitude. It has to be
realised out of Knowledge and Belief.

That makes the tripartite analysis unworkable in two complementary ways.

1. There is no place for a justified false belief. A false belief can be
justified in the ordinary sense and it cannot be Knowledge because Knowledge
entails truth. If justification is not an independent state it can only be
realised as Knowledge or as Belief. If the justifiers for p are required to be
known then to know p you must know that you are justified in believing p,
and to know that you are justified you must know that you are justified in
believing that you are justified, etc. If the justifiers are only believed
you get the familiar circularity/regress: a belief is justified by a belief
in its justification and the justification of that belief must itself be
justified. In taxonomic terms the state ‘justified but false’ is not
Knowledge and it is not mere unqualified Belief; it is a justified Belief
which the two-state ontology cannot register. JTB therefore either has to
deny the possibility of justified false belief or conflate it with ordinary
belief.

2. There is no place for an unjustified true belief. A true belief can be
unjustified and it cannot be Knowledge because Knowledge entails
justification. The state ‘true but unjustified’ is again not Knowledge and,
on the two-state taxonomy, it is not distinguishable from an ordinary
Belief. Once justification has been identified with Knowledge or with Belief
the distinction between a justified true belief and an unjustified true belief
is lost inside the category Belief. In the usual formulation that is the
regress/circularity problem for justification: if justification is itself a
Knowledge state you get an infinite hierarchy of higher order knowledge
know-that-you-are-justified, know-that-you-know-that-you-are-justified...
; if justification is itself merely a Belief you get circular, never
grounded, justification.

Hence with only Knowledge and Belief in the inventory JTB cannot make
room for the intuitively distinct epistemic statuses of justified false
belief and unjustified true belief. The analysis collapses the justified/
unjustified and the true/false dimensions into the single dichotomy
Knowledge vs. Belief. That is the classic regress/circularity of
justification and the taxonomic loss of justified false and unjustified true
beliefs, the Gettier problem being set aside.

3.text:
**PUBLIC RESPONSE:** With only Knowledge = Justified True Belief and Belief left as primitive epistemic kinds the 2 x 2 space of Truth × Justification collapses.

* T & J = Knowledge by JTB
* T & ¬J = Belief
* ¬T & J = Belief
* ¬T & ¬J = Belief

Belief therefore has to do all the work for the three remaining cells and it becomes a heterogeneous grab-bag.

1. **Justification is lost for false beliefs.** A justified false belief is not knowledge because it is not true, so on the JTB taxonomy it must be classified as a mere belief. It is then epistemically indistinguishable from an unjustified false belief and from any other false belief. Intuitively a justified false belief is epistemically better than an unjustified false belief, but JTB with only K/B has no state to mark that difference.

2. **Truth is lost for unjustified beliefs.** An unjustified true belief is not knowledge because it is not justified, so it too must be classified as a mere belief. It is then epistemically indistinguishable from an unjustified false belief and from a justified false belief. Intuitively a true, even lucky, belief is factually better than a false belief, but JTB with only K/B has no state to mark that difference.

The result is that the category ‘belief’ mixes together justified false beliefs with unjustified false beliefs and mixes together true unjustified beliefs with false unjustified beliefs. Truth and justification are each only discriminating inside the belief class, and the independent normativity of justification for false propositions and of truth for unjustified propositions is erased. That is the coarse-graining that is normally remedied by introducing further epistemic states such as justified false belief and true unjustified belief / epistemic luck.

2.text:
Under JTB Knowledge = Justified & True & Believed. With only the two taxonomic boxes Knowledge / Belief everything that is not justified-and-true is put in the Belief box.

That binary taxonomy therefore erases the independence of justification and truth.

* Justified false belief. Justification does not entail truth. There are beliefs that are well justified by the subject’s evidence and yet false. On JTB they are not knowledge because they are not true, so they must be counted as Belief. The state “justified belief” is therefore invisible: a justified false belief is lumped together with an unjustified false belief under the single label Belief.

* Unjustified true belief / lucky true belief. Truth does not entail justification. There are true beliefs that are held by luck, guesswork, testimony taken on trust, etc., with no justification at all. On JTB they are not knowledge because they are not justified, so they must be counted as Belief. The state “true belief” is therefore invisible: an unjustified true belief is lumped together with a false belief under the single label Belief.

Hence with only Knowledge versus Belief you cannot keep the justification dimension separate from the truth dimension. Justified false beliefs and unjustified true beliefs are both forced into the undifferentiated Belief category, so justification can fail to secure truth and truth can obtain without justification, and the taxonomy has no way to mark those two independent defects of belief.

4.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: With JTB Knowledge = Justified ∧ True ∧ Belief. If the taxonomy is only
Knowledge vs. Belief, then every state that is not JTB is by default
‘Belief’. That makes Belief a disjunctive grab-bag

* Belief =  J ∧ ¬T ∧ B  ∨  ¬J ∧ T ∧ B  ∨  ¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B

and it forces two intuitively distinct non-knowledge states to the
same box.

1. Justified false belief. J ∧ ¬T ∧ B is not Knowledge because it is
not true, so on a Knowledge/Belief dichotomy it must be classified as
mere Belief. The justification that is present in the state is therefore
lost in the taxonomy: a justified false belief is put on the same level
as an unjustified false belief and there is no way to mark that it is
epistemically better than the latter.

2. Unjustified true belief. ¬J ∧ T ∧ B is not Knowledge because it is
not justified, so on the dichotomy it must also be classified as mere
Belief. Truth that is present in the state is therefore lost in the
taxonomy: a lucky true belief is put on the same level as a justified
false belief and as an unjustified false belief, and there is no way to
mark that it is epistemically better than the latter two.

Hence Belief has to do the work of justified-but-false, true-but-
unjustified and unjustified-and-false at once. The independent
epistemic value of justification and the independent epistemic value of
truth are both collapsed into the single residual category of Belief,
and we lose the natural distinctions between a justified false belief
and an unjustified false belief and between an unjustified true belief
and a justified false belief. That is why the binary Knowledge/Belief
scheme is normally supplemented with an intermediate justified-belief
category.
